items.claim: setJointWeights rescales by a sum that counts negative and NaN weights, which skinPath and jointShares ignore
TargetTable.refill writes to the caller's options object, and throws when it is frozen
A color cycle replaced or cleared through the registry keeps the frame loop running for good
readTarget hands a custom `axes.add` a shared module-level scratch longer than the target's axis count
A stagger's handle reports its last time scale and pause after it ends, where a loop's reports 1 and unpaused
axisIndexes only refuses a name that is both an axis and a path prefix when `paths` is given, though its doc says it always does
cycleVertexColors with `direction: -1` plays its easing curve backward, so ease-in turns into ease-out
createTargetTable throws an unexplained RangeError for a capacity that is not a whole number
Target-table `remove` of a row twice, or of a row never added, gave two adds the same row
items.note: now b8cf301db1 after the autosquash. `set` and `target` on a row not in use now throw too.

items.claim: Target-table `add` with a wrong-length value leaked a row index
Target-table `target(row)` on a row not in use read past the table
items.note: duplicate of the `remove` finding, fixed in b8cf301db1.

items.claim: Loop/tweenLoop `count` of `NaN`, a fraction or a negative was accepted
A stagger item whose factory throws left the stagger registered for good
items.note: My call: the stagger is canceled along with the items it started, and the throw goes on. Recorded in `docs/unruled.md`.

items.claim: A loop whose factory throws stayed registered and kept the frame loop running
items.note: the same commit and the same rule as the stagger.

items.claim: `createElementTarget` with `get` and no `set`, or `set` and no `get`, dropped commits
`Target.commit` on a target at rest never reached `show`, so an element target's style went stale
items.note: A commit at rest now calls `show`, then `publish`. Core's `bindRig.pose` already showed after its commit; it now does that only while a run is moving the rig, so it doesn't show twice.

items.claim: A joint name with a dot (`spine.001`) came along with `axes: ['spine']`
items.note:
`TargetAxes` gets a new optional `paths` field, so the changeset is `minor`, tagged `fix api`.
  - The same mistake applied to plain-object axes, where a field named `a.b` was reached by `a`; fixed in the same commit.
  - My call: a name that is both one axis's name and the start of another axis's path (`arm.x`) throws. Recorded in `docs/unruled.md`.

items.claim: `jointShares` counted negative and `NaN` weights that the skin never applies
`staggerVertexColors` with `anchorMs: 0` painted `NaN`, and took bad delays and origins unchecked
items.note: `anchorMs: 0` now steps each anchor in turn; a negative or non-finite time or origin throws a `RangeError`.

items.claim: `ColorOverrideRegistry.set` stored the caller's array, so re-setting it after an in-place edit did nothing
items.note: It now keeps a copy. Three tests that asserted the stored array's identity now compare by value.

items.claim: `ColorOverrideRegistry.target` at a new length dropped painted colors without notifying subscribers
`TrimOverrideRegistry.has` said an override with no edges was painting
items.note: A `set` with neither edge now drops the override. The property test's model was updated to match.

items.claim: `cancelAll` stopped a color cycle's frames but left its colors painted
items.note: `keepAlive` takes a new optional `onCancel`, so this changeset is also `minor`, tagged `fix api`.
